To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the acylated and deoxy spinosyns are more potent than the parent compounds, and that spinosyns can tolerate a 2'-desmethyl group, but not a 2'-methoxy or 3'-desmethyl.

the 2'-desmethyl analogs were more potent insecticides, the 3'-desmethyl-O-acetylated analogs were more active than their respective parent factor, but not as active as spinosyn A, and the 4'-desmethyl and 4'-deoxy analogs were less active than their respective factors.

the 2'-desmethyl analog of spinosyn J is the first spinosyn analog with insecticidal activity greater than that of the natural products spinosyns D or A, and that the acylated spinosyns are more potent insecticides, but not as active as spinosyn D.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and insecticidal properties of spinosyn derivatives with altered rhamnose moieties.
the synthesis of spinosyn factors that are functionally altered at 2'-, -3'-, and -4'-positions of rhamnose.
the synthesis of spinosyn derivatives with the aim of improving their insecticidal activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the 2'-O-desmethylene-O-methoxy analogs are the best analogs of spinosyn D and spinosyn A with insecticidal activity against H. vi rescens larvae.
the 2'-O-methyl group of spinosyn is not essential for insecticidal activity, the 2',3'-di-O-methyl group is essential, and that the 4'-O-methyl and 2'-O-acyl group contribute to the potency.
the 4'-O-acetyl and 2'-O-deoxy groups are preferred over the 4'-OH and 2'-OH groups, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the spinosyns are tolerant to a variety of functional groups in the rhamnosyl residue and that the 2'- and 3'-positions are the most tolerant to modifications.
the 2'-position of the rhamnosyl moiety is a major determinant of insecticidal potency in spinosyns and that the 4'-position is the second most important.
analogs with less polarity at the 2', 3' and 4' positions of the rhamose moiety of the spinosins have increased insecticidal activity against H. viersens larvae.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rhamnoso moiety of spinonyn A can tolerate a wide range of functional group changes, and that the insecticidal potency is not necessarily lost by these alterations.
the insecticidal properties of the spinosins are highly dependent on the presence of a 2'-O-methoxymethyl group and the absence of polar functional groups in the rhamnosyl ring of the macrolide.
the 2'- and 4' -O-acetyl analogs are the most potent analogs, with 2'-O-acetyl analog of factor H being the most potent analog against H. vierscens tested to date.
